headline: The tightest block in the set: deep, short and very hard to play through the middle, but it gave Spain the flanks.
good: Most compact team of the twelve: 18 m from front to back and 51 m² of open holes inside the block on average, with only about one Spain player free inside it at a time.
Held its shape for 120 minutes. Block length was 19 m in the first 15 minutes and 18 m in the last 15 of normal time, and the back line barely moved (29 to 31 m).
Kept Spain to 14 shots on 28% possession, and only 2 came within 15 s of Morocco losing the ball.
exploit: Go wide. Spain played through Morocco's lines 103 times, and 64 of those passes arrived on a touchline against 13 through the centre. The block squeezes the middle and gives up the wings.
Get in behind: 48 of those 103 line-breaking passes were received behind the back line. Pedri (23), Jordi Alba (16) and Busquets (12) found the way through most often.
Don't fear the counter-press. Only 28% of Morocco's presses won the ball within 5 s, and just 16% of its ball wins came in Spain's half, so it rarely hurts you high up.

headline: A high line and a fierce counter-press kept Morocco to 6 shots, but the block behind the press was loose.
good: Counter-pressed relentlessly: 170 of its 252 presses came within 3 s of losing the ball, 62 of them winning it straight back. Only Germany pressed more often per minute of defending.
Faced just 6 shots, the fewest of the twelve teams, with a back line pushed 48 m from its own goal (second highest).
Lost the ball in its own half only 22 times all game, so Morocco rarely got to counter from close range.
exploit: Survive the first 3 seconds after winning it. Once the counter-press is beaten there is room: 162 m² of holes inside the block (10th of 12) and about 1.6 Morocco players free inside it.
Play in behind the high line. 33 of the 58 passes through Spain's lines were received behind the back line, often from Hakimi (10) or long from Bono (7).
Attack the wings. Most line-breaks arrived on the flanks (19 on Spain's left, 16 on its right, 8 through the centre).

headline: Went ahead early, sat in a compact block, dropped deeper as the game went on and struck on the break.
good: Third most compact team of the twelve: 98 m² of holes and a 26 m block, with about 1.3 Morocco players free inside it.
Lethal from ball wins: 9 shots within 15 s of winning it (second most of the twelve), and 37 of 108 ball wins were in or into the final third inside 10 s.
No shots conceded from restarts all game.
exploit: Attack France's left side: 30 of the 67 passes through its lines were received on its left wing, Hakimi's flank. Ounahi (15) and Hakimi (14) broke the lines most often.
Be patient. 8 of the 15 shots France faced came from sustained possession rather than quick breaks.
Push it back: France's back line fell from 41 m in the first 15 minutes to 29 m in the last 15, so late on it defends on the edge of its own box.

headline: Took the ball, pushed up and counter-pressed well, but paid for losing it: 10 of the 16 shots it faced came after turnovers.
good: Won the ball high: 41% of its ball wins came in France's half, and 39% of its presses there won it back within 5 s.
Counter-pressed hard: 117 of 220 presses came straight after losing the ball, and 53 won it back. Ounahi and Ziyech led the way.
Had 59% of the ball against the eventual finalists.
exploit: Win it and break. 10 of the 16 shots Morocco faced came after it lost the ball, and 9 of the 16 came within 10 s of the attack starting.
Find the pocket 16-24 m ahead of Morocco's back line: that's where France's players most often stood free inside the block. It was looser here than against Spain (125 m² of holes against 51).
Wait for it to stretch: chasing the game, Morocco's block grew from 25 m to 30 m long in the last 15 minutes and its back line rose from 34 to 40 m.

headline: The most aggressive press and highest line of the twelve, and one of the loosest blocks behind it.
good: Best press in the set: 42% of presses won the ball within 5 s (46% in Japan's half). Havertz (38 presses) and Musiala (32, winning it back 53% of the time) led it.
Won 53% of its ball wins in Japan's half, the highest share of the twelve, with a back line 48 m from its own goal (also the highest).
Kept Japan to 13 shots on 70% possession.
exploit: Beat the first press and the block is wide open: about 1.9 Japan players free inside it (the most of the twelve), 169 m² of holes and a 32 m block (both second worst).
Run in behind. Germany's back line didn't drop at all without the ball, and half of the 44 passes through its lines (22) were received behind it.
Attack Germany's left: 17 of those 44 arrived there, most often from Sakai (9). Late on, chasing the game, its back line went past 60 m.

headline: A deep, compact block that bent a long way (27 shots faced) but didn't break, then turned the game in transition.
good: Second most compact team of the twelve: 80 m² of holes, a 25 m block and about 1.3 Germany players free inside it.
Dropped deeper and tighter once ahead: its back line went from 34 m to 26 m and the block from 25 m to 22 m long in the last 15 minutes.
Stayed patient: 111 ball wins, 30 of them in or into the final third inside 10 s.
exploit: Press its build-up. Japan faced 27 shots, the most of the twelve, and 13 came after it lost the ball. 6 of those were won by Germany in Japan's own third.
Japan's press rarely worked: 26% of presses won the ball within 5 s, the lowest of the twelve, and just 1 in 48 against a carry or first touch.
Switch play to its right side: 26 of 90 line-breaking passes arrived there, with Gündoğan (16), Kimmich (15) and Raum (12) the main sources.

headline: Passive and deep: rarely won the ball high, relied on sitting in its own half, and was got behind easily.
good: Tightened up late: its block shrank from 33 m to 29 m long and its back line dropped from 32 m to 28 m in the last 15 minutes to protect the lead.
Held on for the win despite facing 22 shots.
De Bruyne was its most active presser (39 presses).
exploit: Run in behind: 38 of the 50 passes through Belgium's lines were received behind the back line, the highest share of any team. Johnston (12) and Eustaquio (11) found them most.
Press it without fear of the counter: only 16% of Belgium's ball wins came in Canada's half and it had 21 fast attacks, both the lowest of the twelve.
Win it in midfield: 10 of the 22 shots Belgium faced came after it lost the ball, 5 of them won by Canada in the middle third.

headline: Front-foot and brave: a high line, lots of high ball wins and 22 shots, but the block stretched as the game went on.
good: Won the ball high: 49% of its ball wins came in Belgium's half, with 47 fast attacks (both second best of the twelve) and a back line 46 m from goal.
Jonathan David led the press: 44 presses, and half of them won the ball back within 5 s.
Faced only 10 shots, the third fewest of the twelve.
exploit: Wait for it to stretch: Canada's block grew from 31 m to 35 m long in the last 15 minutes, and it had 161 m² of holes on average (9th of 12).
Go long from the back. Belgium's line-breaks came through Castagne (9), Alderweireld (7) and De Bruyne (7), often straight over the press.
Use set pieces: 5 of the 10 shots Canada faced came after a restart.

headline: Balanced and ruthless in transition: 12 shots straight from ball wins, more than any team in the set.
good: Counter-pressed very well: 41% of presses won the ball within 5 s (78 wins from 169 counter-presses). Álvarez (71 presses) and Messi (52) led it.
Deadly from ball wins: 12 shots within 15 s of winning it, the most of the twelve.
Faced only 12 shots over 120 minutes.
exploit: Press its build-up: 10 of the 12 shots Argentina faced came within 10 s of the attack starting, and 5 came from France winning it high in Argentina's third.
Attack its right side: 20 of the 58 passes through its lines arrived on its right wing, with Theo Hernández (9) the main source.
Pin it back: its back line dropped from 37 m to 32 m late in normal time, the spell when France scored twice in two minutes.

headline: Carved open for long spells: Argentina played through France's lines 101 times, and 64 of those passes got in behind, more than against any other team.
good: Most fast attacks of the twelve: 50 ball wins were in or into the final third inside 10 s.
Pressed well when it chose to: 40% won the ball within 5 s. Mbappé (57 presses) and Kolo Muani (43) led it.
Kept its shape across normal time: back line 36 m in the first 15 minutes and 38 m in the last 15, block 30 m to 28 m long.
exploit: Get in behind: 64 of 101 line-breaking passes were received behind France's back line. Messi (24), Enzo Fernández (14) and Mac Allister (11) played them.
Win it in midfield and go: France faced 23 shots, 15 after losing the ball, 8 of them won by Argentina in the middle third.
Find the space between the lines: about 1.7 Argentina players were free inside France's block at any moment (10th of 12), most often 16-24 m ahead of its back line.

headline: Stood a high line and pressed a lot, but the press rarely won the ball and the block was the longest of the twelve.
good: Held its back line 40 m from its own goal (4th highest of the twelve) and pushed it 3 m further up when Bayern had the ball.
Rarely punished for losing it: only 2 of the 117 times it lost the ball led to a Bayern shot within 15 s.
Maina (57 presses) and Ljubicic (55, winning it back 15 times) drove the press, and 40 of its 112 ball wins came in Bayern's half.
exploit: Play through the first press: only 28% of Köln's presses won the ball within 5 s, among the three lowest of the twelve.
Stretch it: at 32.5 m from front to back, Köln's block was the longest of the twelve, and it grew from 29 m in the first 15 minutes to 34 m in the last 15.
Use restarts: 7 of the 12 shots Köln faced came after a restart. Mazraoui (13) broke its lines most often from open play.

headline: Gave Köln few shots, but left more open space inside its block than any of the twelve teams.
good: Faced just 9 shots, the second fewest of the twelve.
Counter-pressed well: 72 of its 157 counter-presses won the ball back within 5 s, and 38% of all its presses did (5th of the twelve).
Sané's pressing paid off most (19 ball wins from 51 presses); Gnabry pressed most often (56).
exploit: Get between the lines: 174 m² of holes inside the block, the most of the twelve, and about 1.8 Köln players free inside it (second most), most often in the centre just ahead of the back line.
Attack Bayern's left: 30 of the 48 passes through its lines were received on that side (20 on the wing), and 29 of the 48 were received behind the back line. Schmitz (11) broke its lines most often.
Keep going late: its back line fell from 46 m in the first 15 minutes to 37 m in the last 15 of normal time, and the block narrowed from 40 m to 35 m.
